_comment: Phase 2A.12 hardware-assisted validation gate configuration. Consumed by tools/phase2a_hardware_gate.ps1. Docs/tooling artifact - not firmware source.

acceptedBaseline.note: This is the exact commit and CI evidence the Phase 2A acceptance record (docs/PHASE2A_ACCEPTANCE_RECORD.md) covers. Hardware-assisted validation against a different commit is not itself wrong, but should be flagged for review rather than silently treated as validating this same accepted baseline.

expectedArtifacts.note: These are the real, GitHub-Actions-generated values recorded in docs/PHASE2A_ARTIFACT_HASHES.md (Phase 2A.11, finalization run 28859929957) - not fabricated, not archive-level digests. HashVerify/HardwareAssisted modes compare a locally-downloaded artifact directory's actual files against these exact values.

forbiddenTestCategories: Any cloning, brute force, jamming, deauth, or bypass behavior
forbiddenTestCategoriesNote: This script contains no code path for any of the above, for any app, under any flag or mode - this is not a configuration toggle to disable, it is simply not implemented anywhere in tools/phase2a_hardware_gate.ps1.
flashConfirmationPhrase: I UNDERSTAND THIS WILL FLASH THE CONNECTED DEVICE
flashConfirmationNote: The script never performs a flash itself under any circumstance - even after -AllowFlashPrompt and a correctly-typed confirmation phrase, flashing remains a manual, deliberate action performed by the operator using qFlipper or fbt flash_usb outside this script. The confirmation gate exists to make sure the operator has seen the artifact hashes and rollback warning before proceeding, not to automate the flash itself.

deviceDetection.note: Flipper Zero enumerates as a USB CDC-ACM serial device (ST Microelectronics VID 0483, PID 5740) when running normal firmware. Detection uses Windows PnP device enumeration (Get-PnpDevice) only - no serial communication, no RPC, no data exchange with the device.

officialToolingDetection.note: Best-effort detection only (PATH lookup, common install directories, and the Windows uninstall registry key). Absence of a detected install does not necessarily mean qFlipper isn't present under a nonstandard path - it means this script could not confirm it automatically, and flashing tooling should be classified BLOCKED / TOOLING NOT AVAILABLE rather than assumed present.
